public_rationale: OpenAI’s February 2025 release evaluation reports a nonzero hallucination rate for GPT-4.5. That directly supports the ordinary reading that hallucinations persisted in contemporary frontier models. The lower rate than the comparison models also shows why persistence should not be read as an absence of progress.
limitations: PersonQA concerns factual questions about people; its rate is not an estimate for all uses.
These are company-reported evaluations, not an independent replication.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hallucinations have not gone away, even in the latest models.

statement.excerpt: Hallucinations simply haven’t gone away, even in the latest models.
statement.document_title: Ezra Klein’s new take on AGI – and why I think it’s probably wrong

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that contemporary frontier models still sometimes present invented or incorrect factual information as fact.
This does not assert a particular hallucination rate, equal rates across models, or an absence of improvement.
For the ongoing state, use early-2025 evaluations available through the post date, January 1–March 5, 2025. AI capability evaluations have no standard reporting quarter.
criteria.support_condition: A documented evaluation of a contemporary frontier model reports a nonzero rate of factual hallucinations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evaluations establish that contemporary frontier models have eliminated factual hallucinations across relevant uses.
